correctness.rationale: Pair (core v,leaf v′) has weight >=2 in any double Roman function; equality forces (0,2), while weight3 forces (0,3),(1,2),(2,1),(3,0). The core indices with weight>=3 form a dominating set D of G: each outside core has only its private leaf 2 and needs a high core neighbor. Thus weight>=2n+gamma(G), with explicit (2,1) cores on minimum D attaining it and meeting the non-dominating-zero-set maximality condition. Equality gives each D a choice S of high cores (2,1)/(3,0), while D\S uses (1,2)/(0,3), and V\D subset N(S) is exactly the outside-zero defense condition. Maximality excludes precisely the all (3,0)/(0,3) choice, yielding (2^q-1) per admissible (D,S). For C_n, circular gap lengths 1..3 with sum n and q=ceil(n/3) give cases n mod3: 3, n(n+11)/6, n admissible pairs. Independently brute-force checked complete 0..3 vertex labels and zero-set nondomination for K1, K2, K3, C4: optimal weight/count (3,2),(5,2),(7,3),(10,30). This includes isolated and n4 boundary; the source large graph checks and logs were read as corroboration only.
residual_risks: Finite checks include n<=4 examples, not universal correctness proof; the pair-equality classification is essential.
